nodes.label: Never Do These
nodes.rationale: The hard prohibitions: push straight to main, commit secrets, commit real buyer data, force-push a shared branch, and bypass the checks.

nodes.label: Working With AI Coding Agents
nodes.rationale: AI agents are welcome, but the human owns everything they write.

nodes.label: Checklist
nodes.rationale: The closing self-check: one thing and no and in the title; bun run check and bun run format run and CI green; open pull requests checked for overlapping files and related issues linked; the last commit refreshes the Graphify graph; the whole diff read including anything an AI agent wrote; UI follows docs/DESIGN.md with no browser-native inputs or selects; docs updated if behaviour changed; no secrets, .env files or real buyer data.

nodes.label: Follow The Design Guide And Shared UI Components
nodes.norm_label: follow the design guide and shared ui components
nodes.rationale: UI must follow docs/DESIGN.md and use the components in frontend/src/components/ui/, never browser-native inputs, selects or date pickers, so Mortar stays visually consistent and accessible.

nodes.label: Keep AI Agents On Task
nodes.rationale: Ask for one change at a time, matching one issue; large mixed changes from an agent are the fastest way to a messy repo.

nodes.label: Never Force-Push A Shared Branch
nodes.rationale: Never run git push --force on a branch someone else works on, because it silently destroys their commits.

nodes.label: No Pushes Straight To main
nodes.rationale: Always go through a pull request, because the pull request is the last review before the live site.

nodes.label: Never Commit Real Buyer Data
nodes.rationale: No real names, IC numbers, phone numbers or bank details in code, test data, screenshots or issues; all Mortar data is synthetic. See docs/TRD.md#data-retention.

nodes.label: Never Commit Secrets
nodes.rationale: No .env files, API keys, passwords or tokens. Use .env.example for placeholders only, so a placeholder can never be mistaken for a live credential.

nodes.label: One Problem Per Issue
nodes.rationale: If you find a second problem, open a second issue, so each issue stays small enough to review and close.

nodes.label: One Thing Per Pull Request
nodes.rationale: If the title needs the word and, split it. Aim for under about 400 changed lines, not counting bun.lock, so review and revert stay tractable.

nodes.label: Point Agents At The Rules
nodes.rationale: Agents read AGENTS.md, which links back to this guide, so the written rules reach the agent instead of living only in a human's head.

nodes.label: Read The Diff Before Committing
nodes.rationale: Read every changed line before committing. If you cannot explain a change, do not ship it, because unexplained code becomes unreviewable and unmaintainable code.

nodes.label: Update The Docs In The Same Pull Request
nodes.norm_label: update the docs in the same pull request
nodes.rationale: If behaviour changed, update the PRD, TRD or docs/agents/notes.md in the same pull request, so the docs never drift from the deployed behaviour.

nodes.label: Data Check
nodes.rationale: A required checkbox the reporter must tick confirming the report and screenshots contain no real buyer names, IC numbers, phone numbers or bank details. Because screenshots are encouraged, the form pushes the privacy rule to the exact moment a real name could be pasted or photographed into the issue.

nodes.label: graphify affected
nodes.rationale: Lists what a change to something would touch, for example graphify affected "PERSONA_PAGES".

nodes.label: graphify explain
nodes.rationale: Describes one node and its neighbours, for example graphify explain "nextStepFor".

nodes.label: graphify god-nodes
nodes.rationale: Reports the most connected nodes, i.e. the hubs a reader should be careful around when changing something.

nodes.label: graphify path
nodes.rationale: Finds how two things connect, for example graphify path "AskPanel" "createAssistant".

nodes.label: graphify query
nodes.rationale: Walks the graph breadth first and answers a question in words, for example graphify query "how does Today choose each card's next step". Add --dfs to trace one path and --budget N to cap the answer at N tokens, so a search that would otherwise sprawl is bounded.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md is the plain-language overview, for a reader who wants the shape of the repository without running a query.

nodes.label: Ask The Graph First
nodes.rationale: Before searching with grep or opening file after file, query the graph. Fall back to grep only when the graph does not answer, or when exact text or line numbers are needed, because those are the two cases a graph cannot serve.

nodes.label: Graph First, Then Grep
nodes.rationale: Have agents query the Graphify graph (graphify query) before grepping; it answers most questions for far fewer tokens.

nodes.label: What You Expected
nodes.rationale: Required textarea: what should have happened instead, which separates a genuine defect from intended behaviour.

nodes.label: Steps To Reproduce
nodes.rationale: Required textarea asking for the exact steps someone else can follow, with a worked example placeholder (sign in as Sales Admin, open Today, click the first card, see the error) because a bug another person can reproduce is a bug that can be verified and regression-tested.

nodes.label: What Happened
nodes.rationale: Required textarea: what went wrong, including any error message word for word, so the developer can search logs for the exact text.

nodes.label: Where: Live Site / Running Locally / Both
nodes.norm_label: where: live site / running locally / both
nodes.rationale: Required dropdown separating deployed-only faults from local-only faults, which points straight at whether the deploy or the dev environment is at fault.

nodes.label: Pitch Priority
nodes.rationale: Required dropdown asking how much the request matters for the Chin Hin pitch, with options Blocks the pitch, Improves the pitch, After the pitch. It ties ordering to an external deadline rather than to whoever filed first.

nodes.label: How To Check It
nodes.rationale: Numbered steps a reviewer can follow, with a worked example (sign in as Sales Admin, open Today, click the first card), so verification is written down next to the change and can be repeated on the live site after the deploy.

nodes.label: The Journey Of A Change
nodes.rationale: Issue -> Branch -> Commits -> Pull Request -> Review -> Squash Merge -> Live. Each step answers what and why, keeps the branch your own copy, commits in small steps, lets CI check it, needs a teammate approval, lands one commit on main, and confirms the change on the live site.

nodes.label: When Something Breaks On The Live Site
nodes.norm_label: when something breaks on the live site
nodes.rationale: Three steps: tell the team first in chat with a screenshot and page link; revert rather than patch, by clicking Revert on the merged pull request and merging the revert pull request, which restores the last working version within minutes; then fix calmly through a bug issue and a new branch on the normal journey.

nodes.label: Pre-Commit Hook Formats Staged Files
nodes.rationale: The hook formats staged files automatically; if it fails, read the message, fix it and commit again rather than skipping it.

nodes.label: Reviews And Merging
nodes.rationale: The gate between a finished pull request and the live site: one teammate's approval, green checks, every comment answered, squash and merge, branch deleted, live site checked.

nodes.norm_label: contact link: how we ship changes

nodes.label: Type Of Change
nodes.rationale: Checkbox list mirroring the branch and commit types: Feature (a new capability), Fix (something was broken), UI (look and layout only), Docs (documents only), Chore (tooling, dependencies or config).

nodes.label: Answer Every Comment Then Resolve The Thread
nodes.norm_label: answer every comment then resolve the thread
nodes.rationale: Reply or push a fix, then resolve the thread, so no reviewer concern is left silently open at merge time.

nodes.label: Check The Live Site After The Deploy
nodes.norm_label: check the live site after the deploy
nodes.rationale: Open the live site after the deploy finishes and try the change as a real user would, since green CI does not prove the change works in the deployed bundle.

nodes.label: Delete The Branch After Merging
nodes.rationale: Click Delete branch after merging, so the branch list shows only live work and no one branches off an already-merged copy.

nodes.label: Merging Into main Deploys To The Live Site
nodes.norm_label: merging into main deploys to the live site
nodes.rationale: There is no staging step between merging into main and the live site, so a pull request is the last chance to catch a mistake. Everything else in the guide exists to protect that moment.

nodes.label: Green Checks Only
nodes.rationale: Merge only when every check shows a green tick, since merging ships straight to the live site.

nodes.label: Never Merge Your Own Pull Request
nodes.norm_label: never merge your own pull request

nodes.label: One Branch, One Change

nodes.label: Graphify
nodes.rationale: graphify-out/ holds a knowledge graph of the repository. Code files and documents are nodes, imports, calls and references are edges, related nodes are grouped into communities. Asking the graph costs a fraction of the tokens that reading files through repeated searches costs, so agents ask it first.

nodes.label: .graphifyignore
nodes.rationale: Uses .gitignore syntax and applies on top of .gitignore, so a file is only in the graph if neither list excludes it. When a new kind of generated or binary file appears, add it there.

nodes.label: Installing Graphify
nodes.rationale: Install once with uv tool install graphifyy, or pipx install graphifyy, which provides the graphify command. In Claude Code the /graphify skill wraps the same tool, so there is one underlying tool behind two entry points.

nodes.label: graphify update .
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts changed code with no model and no key, so the code half of the graph is cheap to keep current on every change.

nodes.label: What The Graph Leaves Out
nodes.rationale: The ignore list keeps out files with no extractable knowledge: images, video and audio, PDFs and Office files, fonts, archives and binaries, Python bytecode, data dumps, the precomputed Jev cache (server/fixtures/jev-cache.json), lockfiles, vendored agent tooling and the graph itself. Excluding them keeps the node count an honest measure of what the repository actually says.

nodes.label: --force Flag For Node-Count Regression
nodes.rationale: graphify update refuses to write a graph with fewer nodes, a guard against a partial extraction silently shrinking the graph. After a refactor that genuinely deletes code, pass --force to override the guard deliberately.

nodes.label: When To Do A Full Rebuild
nodes.norm_label: when to do a full rebuild
nodes.rationale: Rebuild the whole graph with /graphify . instead of updating it when .graphifyignore changes, or when graphify query cannot find code that is known to exist. A changed ignore list or a missing node means the incremental state can no longer be trusted, so a full pass is the only way back to a correct graph.

nodes.label: Keep It Current
nodes.rationale: The graph is committed to the repository, so main must always carry a current one; a stale graph is worse than none because agents trust it over reading the code.

nodes.label: Never Merge Graph Files By Hand
nodes.norm_label: never merge graph files by hand
nodes.rationale: When two pull requests both change graphify-out/, take either side, run graphify update . again, and commit the result. The graph is a derived artefact, so it is regenerated rather than merged, which cannot produce a graph that matches neither side.

nodes.label: Refresh The Graph As The Last Commit Of Every Pull Request
nodes.norm_label: refresh the graph as the last commit of every pull request
nodes.rationale: Rebase on main, run graphify update ., and commit graphify-out/. Refreshing inside the pull request keeps main current without an extra commit, which would redeploy the prototype.

nodes.label: /graphify . --update Skill For Changed Documents
nodes.rationale: graphify update . covers code only; when a pull request changes documents, also run the /graphify . --update skill, which re-reads changed documents with the model.

nodes.label: Never Bypass The Checks
nodes.rationale: Do not disable a test, lint rule or hook to make a failure go away; ask for help instead, because a disabled check is invisible protection that never runs again.

nodes.label: Refresh The Graphify Graph Last
nodes.rationale: Make graphify update . the last commit so main always carries a current graph. See docs/agents/graphify.md.
